topic: how first-round interviews are run for engineering hires

options.A: replace the phone screen with a 30-minute take-home exercise

versions.option_text: a 45-minute structured video screen, two interviewers scoring against a shared rubric

chain.speaker: Priya
chain.gist: Priya proposes replacing the first-round phone screen for engineering roles with a 30-minute take-home exercise.
chain.option: replace the phone screen with a 30-minute take-home exercise

chain.speaker: Priya
chain.gist: Priya argues that phone screens are inconsistent, since last quarter the pass rate was 38 percent with one recruiter and 61 percent with another, and a take-home gives every candidate the same task.
chain.option: replace the phone screen with a 30-minute take-home exercise

chain.speaker: Aisha
chain.gist: Aisha reports that the data team's take-home last spring lost 46 of 120 invited candidates before they returned it, and those who finished said they spent about three hours.
chain.option: replace the phone screen with a 30-minute take-home exercise

chain.speaker: Diego
chain.gist: Diego proposes a 45-minute structured video screen with two interviewers scoring the same questions against a shared rubric.
chain.option: a 45-minute structured video screen, two interviewers scoring against a shared rubric

chain.speaker: Diego
chain.gist: Diego argues this fixes the consistency problem without the drop-off, at a cost of about 90 interviewer-minutes per candidate against 30 for a phone screen.
chain.option: a 45-minute structured video screen, two interviewers scoring against a shared rubric

chain.speaker: Bashir
chain.gist: Bashir picks the structured video screen for first-round engineering interviews.
chain.option: a 45-minute structured video screen, two interviewers scoring against a shared rubric
